_comment: A sea standing well below the level the terrain left it: coastlines walk out, basins keep a little
water, and the high ground grows.
**`deep`'s antonym, and nothing had to be written to make it one.** `Vocabulary.antonym` finds two
words setting one parameter opposite ways, so the pair is an OPPOSED contradiction on its own. The
`art/antonyms/` table is about preset *tags* and has no business carrying this.
**Gentler than `deep` is, on purpose, and the asymmetry is the honest bit.** -0.7..-0.5 is about twelve
to thirty-three blocks down -- roughly half its usual level at the far end, which is what a drained sea
reads as. Matching `deep`'s reach downward would take the waterline under most landform floors and
leave no sea at all, which is a different word than this one.
**Said of features, it is where they sit: near the surface**, `buried`'s mirror. `shallow veins` are
vanilla's copper veins -- its band and its granite -- where a vein left alone is its deep iron one.
Inside a minting clause the height is that clause's own, as a size is, so the Age's other ores stay put.
